items.text: Selection methods · Fetchers · Spiders · Proxy Rotation · CLI · MCP Scrapling is a Python Web Scraping framework that brings fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, powerful parsing, and concurrent crawling into one library. Scrape static pages, render JavaScript, interact with websites, and extract data from the API calls behind them. Build crawlers with reusable sessions, proxy rotation, automatic retries, pause/resume, and built-in data exports. Use it from Python, the terminal, or your AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill. From extracting a few fields to collecting a whole website as clean Markdown, Scrapling covers the full scraping workflow. - Fetch & interact: Fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, JavaScript rendering, Cloudflare Turnstile/Interstitial handling, persistent sessions, and background API capture. - Parse & extract: CSS, XPath, text and regex search, adaptive element tracking, similar-element matching, and clean Markdown output. - Crawl & export: Concurrent spiders, proxy rotation, retries, AutoThrottle, pause/resume, streaming, ready-made templates, and JSON/JSONL/CSV/XML exports. - Scrape with AI or from your terminal: An MCP server for AI agents to browse and extract data, an Agent Skill, CLI commands, and an interactive shell. Start with a single page: from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher page = Fetcher.get('https://quotes.toscrape.com/') quotes = page.css('.quote .text::text').getall() print(quotes) Or scale up with a spider: from scrapling.spiders import Spider, Response class QuotesSpider(Spider): name = "quotes" start_urls = ["https://quotes.toscrape.com/"] async def parse(self, response: Response): for quote in response.css('.quote'): yield { "text": quote.css('.text::text').get(), "author": quote.css('.author::text').get(), } res...

items.text: 让 AI Agent 够得着它自己上不去的互联网 让你的 Agent 直接搜索和阅读 X、Reddit、YouTube、小红书…… 💬 有问题、想要新平台、或者想看看别人怎么用？来 Discord 聊聊。 点击展开 Agent Reach 让你的 Agent 真正连上互联网，用上它自己够不着的平台和能力。 Claude Code、Codex、Hermes Agent、OpenClaw 这类 CLI Agent 自带搜索和网页读取，但下面这些它们基本够不着： - 要登录才能用的功能：在小红书搜笔记、在 X 查账号动态、读职位详情等。 - 视频里的内容：B站和 YouTube 的字幕，以及 YouTube 视频、小宇宙播客的语音转文字。 - 中文平台：B站、小红书、V2EX、雪球，通用搜索覆盖很差。 - 干净的结构化数据：雪球行情、V2EX 帖子和回复、GitHub 仓库和 issue，拿到的是整理好的内容。 Agent Reach 把这些平台背后的工具替你装好、测好，Agent 一条命令就能用： agent-reach channels # 有哪些渠道、每个渠道能做什么 agent-reach bilibili search "大模型" # agent-reach [参数] agent-reach read https://www.v2ex.com/t/123 # 按链接自动选渠道 - 适用于哪些 Agent？ 一切 Agent 都能用。 - 会碰我的浏览器和账号吗？ 要登录的平台用 Agent Reach 自己的专用浏览器，在后台运行、不弹窗。第一次用某个网站时，会把你 Chrome 里这个网站的登录复制一份过去，原浏览器不变，不读密码库。复制过来的通常是主账号，建议换成小号，做法见下面的"安全性"。详见会话配置。 下表是当前版本的情况。 - 默认：装好就能用；不想要也可以去掉，以后更新不会再加回来。 - 可选：说一句"帮我加上 XX"就开启，需要的软件会自动装好。 - 实验：能用，但平台反爬更严，可能随时失效。 把这句话发给你的 Agent： 帮我安装 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/Agent-Reach/main/docs/install.md 无论是安装还是升级，都只需要这一条命令就行了。 剩下的 Agent 自己做完。过程中你可能会被问到： - 允许它执行命令：如果 Agent 说自己不能运行命令，去它的设置里打开"允许执行命令"。 - 装 uv：uv 是一个安装命令行程序的小工具，不需要管理员密码。电脑上没有的话 Agent 会先装它，会跟你说一声。 - 要不要加可选渠道：装完后 Agent 会告诉你哪些已经能用（B站、V2EX、GitHub、YouTube、网页），以及还能加哪些。你选了再加，也可以以后随时说"帮我加上小红书"，一条命令就装好。 关于登录：部分平台会直接复用你电脑上已有的登录。想换成某个特定账号（比如小号），跟 Agent 说一声就行。Agent 从不替你登录，也不会要你的密码。 ⚠️ PyPI 上叫agent-reach 的包不是本项目，请勿从 PyPI 安装，只用 install.md 里的 GitHub 地址。 Agent Reach 装的所有东西（各渠道的工具、登录、设置）都放在你电脑上同一个文件夹里（~/.agent-reach/ ），不散落到别处。所以升级、管理、删除都很省事，一句话就行。 直接用大白话跟 Agent 说： 出了问题，Agent 会告诉你是哪个平台、什么原因、下一步怎么做。常见问题见 troubleshooting.md。 每个平台的每个动作都有一个按顺序尝试的工具列表。比如读 B站视频先用 bili-cli，失败了自动换 B站公开接口；读网页先用 Jina Reader，再用 Exa。 flowchart LR A[Agent] -->|agent-reach 渠道 动作| B[Agent Reach] B --> C{按顺序尝试} C -->|首选| D[上游工具 1] C -->|失败时备选| E[上游工具 2] D --> F[结果] E --> F F --> A 平台改版、工具失效是...

items.text: 伯乐Skill（Scout Skill）帮你从一堆信源里选出千里马。 AI News Radar 是一个自动更新的 24 小时 AI 更新雷达。 普通用户直接打开网页，看最近 24 小时 AI、模型、开发者工具和技术生态更新。维护者可以 fork 这个仓库，接入自己的 OPML/RSS、公开 feed、静态页面或 AgentMail 邮箱情报。Codex / Claude Code 这类 Agent 可以使用项目内置的 伯乐Skill，继续帮你判断信息源、维护抓取逻辑、部署 GitHub Pages。 这个项目不是“又一个新闻网页”。 它的核心是伯乐Skill，帮你从一堆信源里选出千里马。哪些源值得长期追踪，哪些源适合做成RSS/OPML，哪些源只能接付费的API，哪些源看起来更新很多但实际上跟你长期关注的方面比方AI只占了里面的5%不到。 先判断清楚，再接入。 好新闻分散在各处， 官方博客发一点，更新日志发一点，X 上有人提前爆料，聚合站又把同一个新闻转来转去。 我以为的自己在追前沿，实际每天都在重复三件事， 打开几十个页面，肉眼+人脑过滤重复内容，猜哪条值得看。 伯乐Skill先替你完成第一轮判断，哪些信源是千里马，哪些是噪音。 你可以随意增加信息源，还可以把一个信息源纳入输入范围，先让它在单独的展示区域运行一个月，再判断要不要录入。 AI News Radar从来都不是单纯把信息抓回来， 它更像是一条轻量的新闻pipeline，把来源判断、抓取、去重、AI强相关过滤、信息源健康状态和静态网页发布串起来，上线后不消耗模型额度。 - 追踪官方 AI 节点，OpenAI News、OpenAI Codex Changelog、OpenAI Skills、Anthropic、Google DeepMind、Google AI、Hugging Face、GitHub AI 等 - 读取高信号日报和Newsletter公开来源，例如 AI Breakfast - 读取网页自带的feed，例如 Follow Builders 的 X builders、Anthropic Engineering、Claude Blog、AI podcasts - 同时接入多个公开聚合源，例如 AI HOT，补足普通官方源看不到的盲区 - 支持OPML/RSS批量导入 - 支持AgentMail邮箱订阅高质量AI日报 - 输出24小时双视图， AI强相关 和全量 - 中英双语标题和站点分组 - 兼容飞书文档，追加了WaytoAGI开源社区最近更新日和近7日变化 flowchart LR source["信息源清单"] --> classify["伯乐Skill判断信源类型"] classify --> official["官方 RSS / changelog"] classify --> opml["私人 OPML / RSS"] classify --> publicFeed["公开 GitHub feed / JSON"] classify --> staticPage["公开页面 / Jina 兜底"] classify --> privateMail["AgentMail 邮箱订阅"] classify --> skip["跳过高风险来源"] official --> fetch["抓取与结构化"] opml --> fetch publicFeed --> fetch staticPage --> fetch privateMail --> fetch fetch --> dedup["去重与归一化"] dedup --> filter["AI 强相关过滤"] filter --> status["源健康与覆盖统计"] filter --> data["data/*.json"] status --> data data --> pages["GitHub Pages 网页"] data --> agent["Codex / Claude Code 继续维护"] AI News Radar学习了现代新闻学的技术，不是简单堆信息源，一次性放几万条信息出来等于没用，所以我选择把新闻处理拆成稳定pipeline，抓取，去重，过滤，补充状态，生成静态站点。 在...

Here’s the video of the talk. In this post I’m going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply. Coding agents in November 2025 Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5. With hindsight, this was a consequential model. In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said: Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. They said that tasks that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 just a few weeks ago are now within reach. This held up. Claude Code was 9 months old at that point, having been introduced alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet on February 24th, 2025. Opus 4.5 was the first model I had used with Claude Code where the default result was generally the right thing. I hadn’t been using Claude Code as a daily driver because it didn’t feel reliable enough—I had to correct it often enough that it didn’t feel like a clear accelerant. The new Opus changed that. For most of the coding problems I faced on a daily basis, Opus would get them right. It was clearly faster than working through the problems myself. Also in November, OpenAI released GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex, and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. items.title: Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
items.summary: In the Codename MDASH pilot, GitHub and Microsoft turned thousands of raw AI findings into 99 checked, private reports with suggested fixes for six widely used open source projects. Maintainers have already fixed more than half. The post Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes. appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.text: Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes. In the Codename MDASH pilot, GitHub and Microsoft turned thousands of raw AI findings into 99 checked, private reports with suggested fixes for six widely used open source projects. Maintainers have already fixed more than half. AI has made finding potential vulnerabilities fast and cheap. Fixing them still takes human judgment, and in open source, that work falls to maintainers. Many are already flooded with AI-generated security findings, including duplicates and reports that aren’t vulnerabilities at all. Another raw scan doesn’t help them. Anyone pointing a new model at a project should ask its maintainers first and come with fixes, not just findings. AI shouldn’t add to maintainers’ workload. So, with maintainers, GitHub and Microsoft ran a pilot together: could AI help maintainers ship fixes instead of handing them more findings? GitHub and Microsoft are using Codename MDASH, Microsoft’s multi-model agentic scanning harness, to find and fix security vulnerabilities in widely used open source software, strengthening the foundation that much of the world’s code is built on. items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.summary: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets.
items.text: Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs. An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take. In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets. Redesigned antibodies also retained binding. Specialized models helped supply sequences and select candidates for testing. The models’ written reasoning and code suggest they draw on math, physics, chemistry, and biological knowledge to reason about protein shapes and interactions with other molecules. In a preprint titled GPT‑6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models, we show that our GPT‑6 family of models has intrinsic capabilities for designing new proteins: the models can design new protein structures and sequences without relying on specialized biology models, using only reasoning and general-purpose coding tools. Proteins do much of the work in living cells. They drive the chemical reactions that sustain life, carry oxygen through the blood, and defend the body against infection. Incorrectly shaped proteins can also cause disease and dysfunction. Proteins are made from chains of chemical building blocks called amino acids. The order, or sequence, of these amino acids helps determine how a protein folds into a three-dimensional shape, which in turn influences what it does. items.text: Senior Solutions Engineer A request to modernize an application often starts with a technology question: Which framework should replace the old one? Before you choose, find out what still works. Then collect evidence that can act as a regression net for that behavior and show where modernization is necessary. I used an evidence-first method on four public applications, from a small Node.js game to a large Java enterprise resource planning (ERP) application. Each needed a different treatment, but the way I collected evidence, chose the next experiment, and decided on possible proof points was repeatable. This post walks through that process so you can apply it to one application of your own. It also shows how to encode the procedure in a GitHub Copilot agent skill while keeping architectural judgment with the people responsible for the system. Build evidence before choosing a target The label on an application rarely tells you enough. “Java microservices” doesn’t tell you which Java Development Kit (JDK) runs in production, where that version is pinned, whether the tests execute, or which interfaces other systems depend on. “Legacy monolith” doesn’t tell you whether the business core is broken or whether one retired platform dependency prevents the application from starting. Before you recommend a change, build a small evidence inventory: - Manifests, lockfiles, entry points, and deployable components - Verified commands for installing, building, testing, packaging, and running - Runtime pins in containers, CI workflows, deployment files, and developer tooling - External contracts such as APIs, database behavior, file formats, and user workflows - End-of-life frameworks and dependencies, with evidence that the application still uses them Record uncertainty while you work...

I never expected this challenge to be all that much easier than P ≠ NP. items.title: What VP ≠ VNP Means (In 3 Minutes)
items.summary: Comments
items.text: I assume you know about the P vs. NP problem. But what is this wacky thing Anthropic just posted? You learned how to take a determinant in your linear algebra class: The naive way is fine for matrices, but notice that you need to perform arithmetic operations here. Exercise for the reader is to find the exact number of operations (hint: start with a recurrence relation). Luckily, if you paid attention, you will remember there are faster ways to do this for big matrices, like Gaussian elimination. If we stick only to adding and multiplying, we can still find a determinant in polynomial time (there are better ways, but this is an old, readable method). A related problem to the determinant is finding the permanent. It’s like a determinant without any subtraction: Unlike determinants, there is no known way to compute permanents in polynomial time. Since finding the permanent of a matrix of 0s and 1s is NP-hard (and in fact #P-complete), it would be pretty important if there were a way. What the Anthropic proof that means is that there is no way to do this if we are limited to arithmetic circuits of size polynomial in the input-size, which look like this: This means that for P to equal NP, there must be some trick to computing permanents using AND/OR/NOT on the bits of the input that is better than addition and multiplication. There are many problems where access to Boolean operators is helpful, but it isn’t clear how they would help with the permanent. If you think of a way, go claim your $1 million.

Its GUI was called Workbench. - Amiga User Interface Style Guide - Android Android is a mobile operating system and a rival to iOS. The first style guide I could locate was in 2012. - Android Design - Material Design v1 - Material Design v2 - Design for Android - BlackBerry BlackBerry was a beleagured maker of mobile handsets. - BlackBerry Wireless Handheld User Interface Style Guide - BlackBerry PlayBook Tablet UI Guidelines - BlackBerry Smartphones UI Guidelines - BlackBerry 10 UI Guidelines - CDE Common Desktop Environment (CDE) is a desktop environment for Unix machines, using (and eventually merging with) OSF/Motif widgets. - OSF/Motif Style Guide - Common Desktop Environment: Style Guide and Certification Checklist - CUA Common User Access (CUA) is a late 1980s standard for user interfaces that influenced Windows and OS/2. - System Application Architecture: Common User Access - Object-Oriented Interface Design: IBM Common User Access Guidelines - GEM/TOS Graphics Environment Manager (GEM) is a 1980s operating system/GUI. It was well-known by users of the Atari ST computers, known in these circles as TOS. - GEM User Interface Guidelines - The documentation for TOS - GNOME GNOME is a desktop environment for Linux and BSD operating systems. Note that the versioning number of these guidelines is very confusing. - GNOME Human Interface Guidelines - GNOME Human Interface Guidelines - GNOME Human Interface Guidelines - iOS and iPadOS iOS (previously iPhone OS) is Apple’s mobile operating...
